name: Mount Kenya National Park/Natural Forest
blurb: Equatorial glaciers, giant groundsel and the forest-to-moorland belts of Kenya's water tower.

tip.title: Thin out the hyraxes
tip.text: Rock hyraxes are the main prey of Verreaux's eagle and also feed leopards. Set them to -100% and watch the eagle, leopard and lobelia respond.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Mount Kenya National Park/Natural Forest

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Giant groundsel
nodes.desc: A tree-like rosette plant of the high alpine valleys. Its leaves fold over the central bud at night, keeping it above freezing.

nodes.name: Giant lobelia
nodes.desc: A tall, hairy-spired rosette plant of the afro-alpine zone, one of the giant lobelias adapted to freezing nights.

nodes.name: Mountain bamboo
nodes.desc: Forms a nearly continuous belt above the forest, thinner on the drier north side, and shades out most other plants.

nodes.name: Tussock grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and sedges that cover the moorland glades above the tree line and feed the mountain's grazers.

nodes.name: Montane forest trees
nodes.desc: Podocarpus and other evergreen trees of the cloud forest on the middle slopes, home to monkeys, hyraxes and elephants.

nodes.name: Rock hyrax
nodes.desc: Lives in rocky crevices up to the moorlands and eats plants including lobelia. It is the main prey of Verreaux's eagle.

nodes.name: Southern tree hyrax
nodes.desc: A nocturnal, tree-living hyrax of the forest belt, browsing leaves and twigs.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: Moves through forest and bamboo on the lower slopes and has been recorded feeding on giant groundsel. Fences keep it out of nearby farms.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: Common in the lower forest and glades, grazing grass in herds.

nodes.name: Mantled guereza
nodes.desc: A black-and-white colobus monkey that lives in the forest canopy and eats mainly leaves.

nodes.name: Bushbuck
nodes.desc: A shy antelope of forest edges and thickets that browses leaves and shoots.

nodes.name: Common duiker
nodes.desc: A small antelope found from the forest up into the moorlands, browsing leaves, shoots and fruit.

nodes.name: Augur buzzard
nodes.desc: A common raptor of the mountain slopes and moorland that hunts small mammals and reptiles from the air.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: A mountain scavenger that lives on carrion, especially bones, and nests on cliffs.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: Hunts and scavenges in the forest belt and drives off or scavenges from other predators' kills.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A solitary hunter that lives at every altitude of the mountain, even the alpine zone, preying on hyraxes, antelope and monkeys.

nodes.name: Verreaux's eagle
nodes.desc: A hyrax specialist: in many areas hyraxes make up most of its diet, so its range follows theirs.

nodes.name: Glaciers and snowmelt
nodes.desc: About a dozen small glaciers and alpine tarns feed streams but are shrinking fast and may vanish within decades.

nodes.name: Mountain rain and cloud
nodes.desc: Rainfall on the slopes, heaviest on the south-east, sets the forest and bamboo belts and fills the rivers that supply the region.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Fertile volcanic soils on the lower slopes support the dense vegetation and surrounding farmland.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates that break down dead plants, dung and carcasses.
